observations.title: Tokachidake volcano (Japan)
observations.description: The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that volcanic activity at Tokachidake continued to intensify. Inflation at relatively shallow depths began to be detected in March. Beginning in April there was an increase in sulfur dioxide emissions, a higher frequency of diffuse volcanic emissions and crater glow observed in monitoring cameras, and slightly elevated seismic activity near and around 62-2 Crater. Starting in May volcanic plumes became more frequent and emissions at the Furikozawa fumarole group rose higher. Subsequently, very small-scale eruptions occurred near the 62-2 Crater on 22 July, 5 August, and 6 August. Additionally, there was an increase in large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes originating near the edifice; two occurred on 12 September, bringing the total count over the preceding 30 days to five. At 0930 on 12 September the Alert Level was raised to 3 (on a scale of 1-5) and the public was warned to be cautious within a 3 km radius. Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)
